summary: John B. Carman worked in Indology and religious studies. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 1999) and as director of the Center for the Study of World Religions.

John B. Cobb Jr. is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago. He founded the Center for Process Studies and held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989).

John Beames was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Merchant Taylors' School, East India Company College (1856-1857), and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1856-1857). He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1858 to 1893.

John Borthwick Gilchrist was a linguist and Indologist educated at the Royal High School, George Heriot's School, and the University of Edinburgh. He served at Fort William College (1800-1804), the East India Company, and University College London (~1828-1831).
John Bray specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied under Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang and held a post at the International Association for Ladakh Studies.
John Briggs was an Indologist and historian who was educated at Eton College until 1799. He later served in the East India Company from circa 1801 to 1835.

John Brockington is an Indologist who earned his MA and DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1987) and Emeritus Professor of Sanskrit (attested 1998-2003) at the University of Edinburgh.

John Brough studied Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and at St John's College under Harold Walter Bailey. He was Professor of Sanskrit at SOAS (1948-1967) and Professor at Cambridge (1967-1984).
John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982. He served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

John Burnet worked in philosophy, having studied at the Royal High School, University of Edinburgh (~1880-1882), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1883-1887). He held a post at the University of St Andrews from circa 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist, linguist, and historian educated at the Royal College of Music, Oxford, and Deccan College. He served at Deccan College (~1958-1960) and SOAS, where he was Lecturer (1950) and Reader (1971-1982).
John C. Huntington specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University (attested 1987-1990 and 2000).

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held posts at the University of North Florida (attested 1988), later becoming distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy (attested 2015).

John Campbell Oman was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He worked in the Public Works Department (1866-1877), as Professor at Government College University, Lahore (1877-1897), and as Principal of Khalsa College (1898-1899).
John Capper worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He founded The Ceylon Magazine in 1840 and served as editor of the Ceylon Times from 1858 to 1874.
John Carnac Morris was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the East India Company College from 1815 to 1817. He was appointed to the Madras Civil Service in 1818.
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1790 to 1797. He served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College in 1808.

John Chadwick was a linguist and historian who studied at Corpus Christi College and Cambridge. He worked on the Oxford Latin Dictionary (~1946-1952) and served as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics at Cambridge (1969-1984).

John Clark Archer studied at Hiram College and Yale University (PhD 1922), specializing in religious studies and Indology. He held various posts at Yale between 1914 and 1950, including Hocker Professor of Comparative Religion (1932-1950).
John Clark Marshman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He founded Serampore College in 1818 and directed the affairs of the Serampore Mission in 1819.
